question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

Uluru is the world's largest monolith and Australia's recognisable natural park with an elliptical shape and a circumfrence of around 94 kilometers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Circumfrence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Circumfrence" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Circumference", meaning the boundary/distance around a circle or curved shape. (परिधि)

◦ Example: The circumference of the wheel is 2 metres.

• Spelling key: CIRCUM + FER + ENCE — note the "fer" (from Latin "ferre", to carry).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Elliptical", "Kilometers" and "Monolith" (a single large block of stone) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related geometry words: circumference (around a circle), diameter, radius, perimeter (around a shape). Watch the "-ference" ending (as in reference, preference, difference).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Bulging
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Contracting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bulging" means swelling or sticking out; expanding outward. Its antonym is "contracting", meaning shrinking or becoming smaller. (उभरा हुआ का विलोम — सिकुड़ना)

◦ Example: His pockets were bulging with coins, but by evening they were contracting as he spent them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Swelling" is a synonym of bulging.

• Option 1 "Weeping" (crying) and Option 4 "Hanging" (suspended) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of bulge: swell, protrude, stick out, expand.

• Antonyms: contract, shrink, deflate, cave in.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

This almirah is made up of heavier metal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. heavy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There is no comparison in the sentence (no "than" and no group), so the positive degree "heavy" is correct. "Heavier" (comparative) is wrong without a comparison.

◦ Correct: This almirah is made up of heavy metal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "heaviest" (superlative) and Options 2 & 3 ("most heavier", "most heaviest" — double forms) are all incorrect here.

NOTE

• Degrees of "heavy": heavy – heavier (with "than") – heaviest (with "the"). Use the positive degree when there is no comparison.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Living within our environmental limits is one of the central _________ of sustainable development.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. principles.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Principles" (a plural noun) means fundamental truths, rules or guiding ideas. Living within environmental limits is one of the guiding ideas (principles) of sustainable development. (सिद्धांत)

◦ Correct: ... is one of the central principles of sustainable development.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "agencies" (organisations) does not fit the sense of a guiding idea.

• Options 3 "demonstrates" and 4 "illuminates" are verbs and cannot follow "one of the central".

NOTE

• Do not confuse principle (a rule/belief — noun) with principal (main / head of a school). Here we need the noun "principles".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Monika said to her mother that, "I have passed the examination."
option_1: Monika said to her mother that, "I am passed
option_2: Monika said to her mother, "I have passed
option_4: Monika said to her mother that, "she has passed
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Monika said to her mother, "I have passed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In direct speech, we do not use "that" before the quoted words, and the exact words are enclosed in quotation marks. So "said to her mother that, "I have passed"" is wrong; it should be "said to her mother, "I have passed"".

◦ Correct: Monika said to her mother, "I have passed the examination."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong "that" and changes to "I am passed".

• Option 4 keeps "that" and wrongly changes "I" to "she".

NOTE

• Direct speech: reporting verb + comma + "exact words in quotes" (no "that"). Indirect speech: reporting verb + that + reported clause (no quotes) — e.g., Monika said that she had passed the examination.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Tara was late for the meeting / but somehow managed / to catch out with / everything she had missed.
option_2: Tara was late for the meeting
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to catch out with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "catch up with", meaning to reach the same level / cover the work or information one has missed. "Catch out" means to expose someone's mistake, which does not fit.

◦ Correct: ... but somehow managed to catch up with everything she had missed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Tara was late for the meeting", "but somehow managed" and "everything she had missed" are all correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "catch": catch up (with) = reach the same point / make up for lost time; catch on = become popular / understand; catch out = expose a mistake.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

I don't prefer to remain alone at home in the evenings because loneliness evokes a sense of melancholy and grief within me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cheerfulness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Melancholy" means a deep, pensive and long-lasting sadness. Its antonym is "cheerfulness", meaning a state of happiness and good spirits. (उदासी का विलोम — प्रसन्नता)

◦ Example: The gloomy weather filled her with melancholy, but the music brought back her cheerfulness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Readiness", Option 2 "Absoluteness" and Option 3 "Shyness" are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of melancholy: sadness, gloom, sorrow, dejection, despondency.

• Antonyms: cheerfulness, happiness, joy, gaiety, delight.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase to fill in the blank.

My car _______ on the way to college yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. broke down.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "break down" means (of a machine/vehicle) to stop working/functioning. So "My car broke down on the way to college." (खराब हो जाना)

◦ Example: The bus broke down in the middle of the road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "broke in" (to enter forcibly / interrupt), Option 2 "broke up" (to end a relationship / disperse) and Option 4 "broke out" (to start suddenly — e.g., a fire/war) do not fit a vehicle failing.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "break": break down (stop working / collapse), break in (enter by force), break out (start suddenly), break up (end/separate), break off (discontinue).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Never _________ ever seen a more disgusting sight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. have I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a sentence begins with a negative adverb like "Never", the word order is inverted — the auxiliary comes before the subject. With the present perfect ("seen"), the auxiliary is "have", giving "Never have I ... seen".

◦ Correct: Never have I ever seen a more disgusting sight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "did I" would need the base verb "see", not "seen".

• Option 2 "has I" is wrong subject–verb agreement ("I" takes "have").

• Option 4 "I have" has no inversion, which is required after the initial "Never".

NOTE

• Inversion after negative openers: Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly, Little, No sooner. "Never have I seen", "Rarely does he speak", "Hardly had she left".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Good nutrition is the bedrock at child survival, health and development.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bedrock of child survival.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "bedrock" (the foundation/basis of something) collocates with the preposition "of" — "the bedrock of something". So it should be "the bedrock of child survival".

◦ Correct: Good nutrition is the bedrock of child survival, health and development.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "bedrock at / from / off child survival" all use wrong prepositions.

NOTE

• "Bedrock" means the fundamental basis. Collocation: "the bedrock of (something)". Synonyms: foundation, basis, cornerstone, groundwork.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Roger applied the __________ in advance as he anticipated an accident.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. brake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "brake" is the device used to slow down or stop a vehicle. Anticipating an accident, Roger applied the brake. (ब्रेक — गति रोकने का उपकरण)

◦ Example: She pressed the brake to stop the car at the signal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "broke" (past of break) and Option 3 "break" (to shatter / a pause) are homophones but wrong in meaning.

• Option 4 "brig" (a type of ship / a prison) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Homophones: brake (of a vehicle) and break (to shatter / an interval). "Apply the brake" (to stop) vs "take a break" (a rest).

question:
Select the most appropriate word from the given options that can substitute the word 'courage' and make a meaningful sentence.

I am not courage enough to take this risk.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. courageous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the linking verb "am" and before "enough", an adjective is required. "Courageous" is the adjective form (brave), giving a correct sentence. "Courage" is a noun and is wrong here.

◦ Correct: I am not courageous enough to take this risk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "encourage" (to give support — verb) and Option 4 "discourage" (to dishearten — verb) are verbs.

• Option 3 "discouraging" (an adjective/participle) has the opposite meaning.

NOTE

• Word forms: courage (noun), courageous (adjective), courageously (adverb). After "be + ___ + enough", use an adjective (brave enough, strong enough, courageous enough).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She was barking up the wrong _______ when she filed a complaint against ragging with the students' union instead of the university administration.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. tree.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to bark up the wrong tree" means to pursue a mistaken or misguided course of action; to blame or approach the wrong person/place. Filing a complaint with the wrong body fits this idiom. (गलत दिशा में प्रयास करना)

◦ Example: If you think I broke the vase, you're barking up the wrong tree — I wasn't even here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "bark up the wrong disc/dog/pillar" are not valid idioms; only "tree" completes it.

NOTE

• The idiom comes from hunting dogs that bark at the base of the wrong tree, thinking their prey is there. It means to direct one's efforts or accusations mistakenly.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Spectaculor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Spectaculor" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Spectacular", meaning very impressive, striking or dramatic. (शानदार / भव्य)

◦ Example: We watched a spectacular display of fireworks.

• Spelling key: SPEC + TAC + U + LAR — the ending is "-ular" (as in popular, regular, circular), not "-ulor".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Enthusiastic", "Gracious" and "Reliable" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Adjectives ending in "-ular": spectacular, popular, regular, circular, particular, molecular. Related: spectacle (noun), spectacularly (adverb).

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Playing in the field, the young gayer students were laughing and giggling.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. gay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There is no comparison in the sentence, so the positive degree "gay" (meaning "cheerful/merry" in this literary sense) is correct, not the comparative "gayer".

◦ Correct: Playing in the field, the young gay (cheerful) students were laughing and giggling.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most gay" and Option 3 "gayest" are superlatives; Option 4 "more gay" is comparative — none is needed without a comparison.

NOTE

• Use the positive degree of an adjective when no comparison is being made. Here "gay" is used in its older literary sense of "light-hearted and cheerful".

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The sky appeared to be greyest after the storm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. grey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There is no comparison among three or more things, so the superlative "greyest" is wrong. The simple positive degree "grey" is correct.

◦ Correct: The sky appeared to be grey after the storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more grey" and Option 2 "greyer" are comparatives (need "than"); Option 3 "most grey" is another superlative.

• After the linking verb "appeared to be", we simply describe the sky with the positive adjective "grey".

NOTE

• Use the positive degree when describing a quality without comparison: "The sky is grey", "The water is cold", "The room looks clean".

question:
The sentence below contains errors. Select the option with the correct use of tenses.

Your father will waiting for you when you reach home.
option_1: Your father should waiting for you when you reach home.
option_2: Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home.
option_3: Your father would waiting for you when you reach home.
option_4: Your father waiting for you when you reach home.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The future continuous tense is formed as will + be + verb-ing. So "will waiting" must be "will be waiting". This correctly expresses an action that will be in progress at a future time.

◦ Correct: Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 ("should waiting", "would waiting", "father waiting") all lack the "be" and use wrong/incomplete verb forms.

NOTE

• Future continuous = will/shall + be + V-ing (will be waiting). Note the subordinate clause "when you reach home" uses the simple present (not "will reach") to refer to the future.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

The future looks bleak for the fishing industry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Depressing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bleak" means not hopeful or encouraging; gloomy and depressing. Its closest synonym is "depressing". (निराशाजनक / उदास)

◦ Example: After the crop failure, the farmers faced a bleak/depressing future.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ample" (plentiful), Option 2 "Expensive" (costly) and Option 3 "Fearless" (brave) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of bleak: dismal, gloomy, dreary, depressing, hopeless.

• Antonyms: bright, promising, hopeful, cheerful. "Bleak" also describes bare, cold, exposed places (a bleak landscape).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Blend
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mix.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Blend" means to mix two or more things together thoroughly. Its closest synonym is "mix". (मिश्रण करना / मिलाना)

◦ Example: Blend/Mix the flour and sugar before adding the eggs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Disperse" (to scatter) and Option 4 "Divide" (to separate) are antonyms in this sense.

• Option 2 "Boil" (to heat to bubbling) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of blend: mix, combine, merge, mingle, fuse.

• Antonyms: separate, divide, disperse, part.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Gourment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gourment" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Gourmet", meaning a connoisseur of good food / relating to high-quality, fine food. (पेटू / उत्तम भोजन का शौकीन)

◦ Example: The restaurant is famous for its gourmet dishes.

• Spelling key: GOUR + MET — it ends in "-met" (the "t" is silent), borrowed from French.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Eligible" (qualified/suitable), "Poignant" (evoking sadness) and "Relevant" (connected to the matter) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• French-origin food words with tricky spellings: gourmet, cuisine, hors d'oeuvre, restaurant, connoisseur, buffet. Do not confuse "gourmet" (fine food lover) with "gourmand" (a greedy eater).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Traditional medicines (TMs) make (1)_______ natural products and are of great importance. Such forms of medicine as traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), Ayurveda, Kampo, traditional Korean medicine (TKM), and Unani (2)_______ natural products and have been (3)_______ all over the world for hundreds or even thousands of years, and they (4)_______ blossomed into orderly-regulated systems of medicine. In their various forms, they may have certain defects, but they (5)_______ still a valuable repository of human knowledge.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. use of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "make use of" means to utilise / employ (something). So "Traditional medicines make use of natural products". The subject "medicines" is plural, so the base verb "make" is correct. (उपयोग करना)

◦ Correct: Traditional medicines make use of natural products.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "used off" and Option 4 "used of" are grammatically wrong.

• Option 3 "uses of" wrongly makes the verb singular (medicines is plural).

NOTE

• "Make use of" is a fixed expression = to use/utilise. Similar: make fun of, make sense of, take care of, take advantage of.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Traditional medicines (TMs) make (1)_______ natural products and are of great importance. Such forms of medicine as traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), Ayurveda, Kampo, traditional Korean medicine (TKM), and Unani (2)_______ natural products and have been (3)_______ all over the world for hundreds or even thousands of years, and they (4)_______ blossomed into orderly-regulated systems of medicine. In their various forms, they may have certain defects, but they (5)_______ still a valuable repository of human knowledge.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. employ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is a list of medicine systems (TCM, Ayurveda, Kampo, TKM and Unani), which is plural, so the verb takes the base form "employ" (use) in the simple present. (प्रयोग करते हैं)

◦ Correct: ... TCM, Ayurveda, Kampo, TKM and Unani employ natural products ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "employs" is singular (wrong for a plural subject).

• Option 2 "employing" and Option 4 "employed" do not fit as the main verb of this present-tense clause.

NOTE

• A compound/plural subject takes a plural verb (base form): "The systems employ..." (not "employs"). "Employ" here means to use/make use of.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Traditional medicines (TMs) make (1)_______ natural products and are of great importance. Such forms of medicine as traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), Ayurveda, Kampo, traditional Korean medicine (TKM), and Unani (2)_______ natural products and have been (3)_______ all over the world for hundreds or even thousands of years, and they (4)_______ blossomed into orderly-regulated systems of medicine. In their various forms, they may have certain defects, but they (5)_______ still a valuable repository of human knowledge.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. practised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "have been ___" requires the past participle (V3) to form the present perfect passive — "have been practised all over the world". (अभ्यास किया गया है)

◦ Correct: ... and have been practised all over the world for hundreds ... of years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "practice" (noun/US verb), 3 "practises" and 4 "practices" are present-tense/noun forms that cannot follow "have been".

NOTE

• Present perfect passive = has/have been + past participle. In British English, "practise" is the verb and "practice" is the noun; the past participle is "practised".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Traditional medicines (TMs) make (1)_______ natural products and are of great importance. Such forms of medicine as traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), Ayurveda, Kampo, traditional Korean medicine (TKM), and Unani (2)_______ natural products and have been (3)_______ all over the world for hundreds or even thousands of years, and they (4)_______ blossomed into orderly-regulated systems of medicine. In their various forms, they may have certain defects, but they (5)_______ still a valuable repository of human knowledge.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "they" (the systems of medicine) is plural, and the present perfect tense is needed to match "have been" earlier. So "they have blossomed into orderly-regulated systems". (परिवर्तित हो गए हैं)

◦ Correct: ... and they have blossomed into orderly-regulated systems of medicine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "has" is singular (wrong for "they").

• Option 1 "have being" is ungrammatical; Option 3 "had" (past perfect) breaks the present-perfect sequence.

NOTE

• Present perfect: has (singular) / have (plural) + past participle. "They have blossomed", "It has blossomed".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Traditional medicines (TMs) make (1)_______ natural products and are of great importance. Such forms of medicine as traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), Ayurveda, Kampo, traditional Korean medicine (TKM), and Unani (2)_______ natural products and have been (3)_______ all over the world for hundreds or even thousands of years, and they (4)_______ blossomed into orderly-regulated systems of medicine. In their various forms, they may have certain defects, but they (5)_______ still a valuable repository of human knowledge.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. are.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "they" (traditional medicines) is plural, and the sentence is a general present truth, so the plural present verb "are" is correct. (हैं)

◦ Correct: ... but they are still a valuable repository of human knowledge.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was" (past singular), Option 3 "am" (used only with "I") and Option 4 "is" (present singular) do not agree with the plural "they".

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: "they/we/you are", "he/she/it is", "I am". Here "they are still a valuable repository" is a general present statement.

question: The liquid water present in oceans, lakes and rivers gets converted to the gaseous form in the presence of sunlight in the water cycle. This step is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Evaporation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Evaporation" is the process by which liquid water changes into water vapour (gaseous form) on being heated by sunlight. It is the first step of the water (hydrological) cycle. (वाष्पीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other steps of the water cycle:

◦ Condensation — water vapour cools and forms tiny droplets/clouds.

◦ Precipitation — water falls back to the Earth as rain, snow or hail.

◦ Collection/Runoff — water gathers in oceans, rivers and lakes, and the cycle repeats.

• Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plants.

NOTE

• Evaporation is a surface phenomenon occurring at all temperatures; boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature. Together, evaporation and transpiration are called evapotranspiration.

question: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on the birth anniversary of which of the following freedom fighters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swachh Bharat Mission (Clean India Mission) was launched on 2 October 2014, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, who dreamt of a clean India. (स्वच्छ भारत मिशन — गांधी जयंती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The mission aimed to achieve an open-defecation-free (ODF) India and improve solid waste management. Its target was to fulfil this vision by 2 October 2019, Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary.

• It has two sub-missions: Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) — rural, and Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban).

NOTE

• 2 October is also observed as the International Day of Non-Violence in Gandhi's honour. The mission's mascot symbol is Gandhi's spectacles.

question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of Hindu population in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, among the given options, Himachal Pradesh had the highest percentage of Hindu population (about 95%). (हिमाचल प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक हिंदू जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• States with a very high Hindu population share also include Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh.

• As per Census 2011, Hindus formed about 79.8% of India's total population.

NOTE

• The Census of India records data on religion, language, literacy, sex ratio, etc. It is conducted every 10 years by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

question: Bharatanatyam Guru __________ received the Nrithya Seva Ratna award from Indian Fine Arts Akademi, San Diego in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hema Rajagopalan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatanatyam Guru Hema Rajagopalan received the Nrithya Seva Ratna award from the Indian Fine Arts Academy, San Diego in 2023 for her contribution to the classical dance form. (हेमा राजगोपालन — नृत्य सेवा रत्न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• It is characterised by fixed upper-body postures, mudras (hand gestures) and expressive abhinaya.

NOTE

• Famous Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, T. Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Padma Subrahmanyam.

question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India mentions that every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in and participate in the proceedings of either House of Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 88.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 88 provides that every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in, and take part in the proceedings of, either House of Parliament (and any joint sitting or committee), but without the right to vote (unless they are a member of that House). (अनुच्छेद 88)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 76 — provides for the Attorney-General of India, the highest law officer, appointed by the President.

• Article 86 — right of the President to address and send messages to Parliament.

• Article 87 — special address by the President (at the opening of the first session).

NOTE

• The Attorney-General has the right of audience in all courts of India and can participate in Parliament, but cannot vote there.

question: The training academy for Indian Police Service officers has been named after:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The training academy for Indian Police Service (IPS) officers is the "Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (SVPNPA)", located in Hyderabad, named after Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. (सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल राष्ट्रीय पुलिस अकादमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the "Iron Man of India", was independent India's first Home Minister and Deputy Prime Minister, and is credited with the integration of princely states.

• The training academy for IAS officers is the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA) at Mussoorie.

NOTE

• Patel's birthday, 31 October, is celebrated as National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas). The Statue of Unity (world's tallest statue) in Gujarat is dedicated to him.

question: Who is revered as 'Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Purandara Dasa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Purandara Dasa is revered as the "Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha" (the Grandfather/Father of Carnatic music). He systematised the teaching methods of Carnatic music and composed thousands of devotional songs (keertanas/devaranamas). (कर्नाटक संगीत पितामह — पुरंदर दास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Purandara Dasa (16th century) is credited with introducing the basic lessons/exercises (like Sarali Varisai) still used to teach Carnatic music.

• The Trinity of Carnatic music are Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri (18th–19th century).

NOTE

• Carnatic music is the classical music tradition of South India; Hindustani music is that of North India. Both are based on raga and tala.

question:
Which of the following statements about nutrients are correct?

Statement A: C, H, O, N, P and K are macro nutrients.  Statement B: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo are micronutrients.  Statement C: Micronutrients are not essential for our body.
option_1: All statements A, B and C
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only statements A and B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement A is correct: C, H, O, N, P and K (carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) are macronutrients — required in large amounts.

• Statement B is correct: Fe, Mn, Ni, Co and Mo (iron, manganese, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum) are micronutrients — required in small (trace) amounts.

• Statement C is WRONG: micronutrients ARE essential for the body (in small quantities); they are needed for proper functioning, so they are not "non-essential".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3 (only A and B are correct).

Additional Information

• Deficiency of micronutrients causes disorders — e.g., iron deficiency → anaemia; iodine deficiency → goitre.

NOTE

• Macronutrients (needed in large amounts): carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and elements like C, H, O, N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S. Micronutrients (trace elements/vitamins): Fe, Zn, Cu, Mn, I, etc.

question: The campaign 'Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath' is associated with which occasion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi Jayanti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cleanliness campaign "Ek Tareekh, Ek Ghanta, Ek Sath" (One Date, One Hour, Together) was a mass shramdaan (voluntary labour) drive for cleanliness held on 1 October 2023, ahead of Gandhi Jayanti (2 October). (एक तारीख, एक घंटा, एक साथ — गांधी जयंती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The campaign was part of the Swachh Bharat Mission, calling upon citizens to devote one hour to cleanliness on the same date and time.

• It aligned with Mahatma Gandhi's vision of a clean India.

NOTE

• Related cleanliness initiatives: Swachh Bharat Mission (2014), Swachhata Hi Seva campaign. Gandhi Jayanti (2 October) is a national holiday.

question: Below are two chemical equations: Zn (s) + CuSO₄ (aq) → ZnSO₄ (aq) + Cu (s); Pb (s) + CuCl₂ (aq) → PbCl₂ (aq) + Cu (s). Why does copper get separated from its compound form in both the cases?
option_1: Zinc and Lead are unstable in element form.
option_2: Copper compounds break down under high pressure.
option_3: Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.
option_4: Copper is more reactive than Zinc and Lead.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In both reactions, copper is displaced from its salt because zinc (Zn) and lead (Pb) are more reactive than copper (Cu). A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution — this is a displacement reaction. (विस्थापन अभिक्रिया — Zn, Pb अधिक क्रियाशील)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the reactivity (activity) series (most → least reactive): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au. Both Zn and Pb lie above Cu, so they can displace it.

• Example: iron displaces copper from copper sulphate (the blue colour fades and a reddish-brown deposit forms).

NOTE

• A displacement reaction: A + BC → AC + B (where A is more reactive than B). This principle is used in the extraction of metals and in electrochemical cells.

question: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chloroplast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, the "Chloroplast" possesses its own DNA (and ribosomes) and can synthesise some of its own proteins. Such organelles are called semi-autonomous organelles. (हरितलवक — अपना डीएनए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other semi-autonomous organelle is the mitochondrion (both chloroplasts and mitochondria have their own DNA — this supports the Endosymbiotic Theory).

• Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis in plant cells.

NOTE

• Chloroplasts (and mitochondria) are believed to have originated from free-living prokaryotes that were engulfed by early eukaryotic cells (Endosymbiotic Theory by Lynn Margulis).

question: Who among the following is/was a famous proponent of Bharatanatyam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was a famous exponent and reviver of Bharatanatyam. She played a key role in bringing respectability and revival to the dance form and founded the institution "Kalakshetra" in Chennai. (भरतनाट्यम — रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She was also a member of the Rajya Sabha and worked for animal welfare; she was reportedly offered the post of President of India but declined.

• Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu (earlier called Sadir/Dasiattam).

NOTE

• Sunanda Nair and Kalavati Devi are associated with Mohiniyattam; Kumkum Mohanty is an Odissi dancer. Rukmini Devi is specifically linked with Bharatanatyam.

question: In the Great Stupa at Sanchi there are _______ gateways known as 'Toranas' at the cardinal points to the compass.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh) has four gateways (Toranas), one at each of the four cardinal directions (North, South, East and West). These toranas are richly carved with scenes from the life of the Buddha and the Jataka tales. (सांची स्तूप — चार तोरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• A stupa is a hemispherical structure containing relics, used as a place of Buddhist worship.

NOTE

• Parts of a stupa: Anda (dome), Harmika (railing on top), Yashti (central pillar), Chhatra (umbrella) and Torana (gateways). The Sanchi lion capital motifs relate to the State Emblem of India.

question: 'Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections' comes under which Article of Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 46.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 46 of the Constitution directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections, and to protect them from social injustice and exploitation. (अनुच्छेद 46)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 46 is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), Part IV of the Constitution.

• DPSPs (Articles 36–51) are non-justiciable but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

NOTE

• Related welfare provisions: Articles 15(4), 16(4), 330, 332, 335, 338, 340, 341, 342 deal with reservations and safeguards for SCs, STs and backward classes.

question: Who among the following has written 'Gita Govinda', a Sanskrit epic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jayadeva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gita Govinda" is a famous Sanskrit lyrical work composed by the 12th-century poet Jayadeva. It describes the divine love between Radha and Krishna. (गीत गोविंद — जयदेव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jayadeva was a court poet of the Sena king Lakshmana Sena of Bengal.

• The Gita Govinda has deeply influenced Indian classical dance (especially Odissi) and devotional (Bhakti) traditions.

NOTE

• Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini (history of Kashmir). Author–work pairs are commonly asked in SSC: Harshacharita (Banabhatta), Mudrarakshasa (Vishakhadatta), Prithviraj Raso (Chand Bardai).

question: Who were the first foreign rulers of northwest India in the post-Mauryan period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bactrian Greeks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the post-Mauryan period, the Bactrian Greeks (Indo-Greeks) were the first foreign rulers to invade and rule over north-western India. (उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत के प्रथम विदेशी शासक — बैक्ट्रियन/इंडो-यूनानी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The most famous Indo-Greek ruler was Menander (Milinda), who embraced Buddhism (recorded in the "Milinda Panha", his dialogue with the monk Nagasena).

• The Indo-Greeks were the first to issue gold coins in India and introduced Hellenistic (Gandhara) art.

NOTE

• Sequence of foreign invaders in the north-west after the Mauryas: Indo-Greeks (Bactrian Greeks) → Sakas (Scythians) → Parthians (Pahlavas) → Kushanas.

question: As of 2023, what is the number of major public seaports in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 2023, India had 12 major (public) ports, which are administered by the Central Government under the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021. (12 प्रमुख बंदरगाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 12 major ports are: Kandla (Deendayal), Mumbai, JNPT (Nhava Sheva), Mormugao, New Mangalore, Cochin, Chennai, Ennore (Kamarajar), V. O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin), Visakhapatnam, Paradip and Kolkata (including Haldia).

• Major ports are managed by the Centre, while non-major (minor/intermediate) ports are managed by the respective State Governments.

NOTE

• India has a long coastline of about 7,500 km. Kandla/Deendayal Port (Gujarat) handles the largest cargo volume; JNPT (Mumbai) is the largest container port.

question: In cycling, what is a 'peloton'?
option_1: The finish line of a race
option_2: A cycling technique for climbing hills
option_3: A group of riders in a tight pack during a race
option_4: The starting line of a race
solution_text:
The correct answer is A group of riders in a tight pack during a race.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In cycling, a "peloton" is the main group/pack of riders bunched together during a race. Riding closely in a pack helps the cyclists save energy by reducing air/wind resistance (drafting). (पेलोटन — साइकिल दौड़ में सवारों का समूह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The word "peloton" comes from French, meaning "a small ball / platoon".

• Famous cycling races: the Tour de France, the Giro d'Italia and the Vuelta a España.

NOTE

• "Drafting" (riding closely behind another) reduces wind resistance, which is why the peloton moves faster and more efficiently than a lone rider.

question: Which author wrote the Hindi novel 'Tamas'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhisham Sahani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Tamas" (Darkness) was written by Bhisham Sahani. It powerfully depicts the communal violence and human suffering during the Partition of India in 1947. (तमस — भीष्म साहनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Tamas" won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1975 and was later made into a famous television series by Govind Nihalani.

• Bhisham Sahni was awarded the Padma Bhushan; his autobiography is "Aaj ke Ateet".

NOTE

• Other famous Hindi writers: Premchand (Godan, Gaban), Shrilal Shukla (Raag Darbari), Yashpal (Jhootha Sach). Bhisham Sahni was the younger brother of actor Balraj Sahni.

question: As of July 2023, 137 unique products under 'One District, One Product' scheme has been notified from how many districts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 713.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2023, under the "One District, One Product (ODOP)" initiative, 137 unique products had been notified across about 713 districts of the country. (एक जिला, एक उत्पाद — 713 ज़िले)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ODOP initiative aims to promote and give recognition to a distinctive local product from each district, boosting local manufacturing, employment and exports.

• It is aligned with the "Vocal for Local" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat" vision and is coordinated by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

NOTE

• ODOP examples: Bhagalpur silk (Bihar), Firozabad glassware (UP), Kanchipuram silk (Tamil Nadu). It is often linked with GI (Geographical Indication) tags.

question: What is the height of the Kanchenjunga peak of Himalaya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8598 metres.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kanchenjunga, at a height of about 8,598 metres (8,586 m), is the highest mountain peak in India and the third-highest in the world. It lies on the border of Sikkim (India) and Nepal. (कंचनजंगा — 8598 मीटर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Kanchenjunga" means "The Five Treasures of Snow" (it has five peaks).

• The highest peak in the world is Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), on the Nepal–Tibet border.

NOTE

• The Kanchenjunga National Park in Sikkim is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kanchenjunga is revered by the people of Sikkim as a sacred mountain.

question: In which of the following years was the Census Act enacted and extended to the whole of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1948.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census Act was enacted in 1948 and extended to the whole of India, providing the legal framework for conducting the census and collecting demographic data. (जनगणना अधिनियम — 1948)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first census of India was conducted in 1872 (under Viceroy Lord Mayo), and the first complete/synchronous census in 1881 (under Lord Ripon).

• The census is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

NOTE

• The Census Act, 1948 makes the giving of information to the census-taker mandatory, while keeping the individual data confidential.

question: What is the usual treatment on repo rates by the Reserve Bank of India in case of a hawkish monetary policy stance?
option_2: Reduced sharply by more than 100 bps
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increased.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a "hawkish" monetary policy stance, the central bank (RBI) prioritises controlling inflation, and therefore usually increases the repo rate. A higher repo rate makes borrowing costlier, reduces money supply and helps curb inflation. (कठोर/हॉकिश रुख — रेपो दर में वृद्धि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks.

• A "dovish" stance (opposite of hawkish) focuses on promoting growth and usually involves cutting/lowering the repo rate to boost the economy.

NOTE

• Monetary policy tools of the RBI: Repo rate, Reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR, MSF, Bank rate. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decides the repo rate to target inflation (currently 4% ± 2%).

question: Who among the following was India's first cricket team captain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CK Nayudu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Colonel C. K. Nayudu (Cottari Kanakaiya Nayudu) was India's first Test cricket captain. He led India in its first-ever Test match against England at Lord's in 1932. (सी.के. नायडू — भारत के पहले टेस्ट कप्तान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• C. K. Nayudu was the first recipient of the Padma Bhushan among cricketers (1956).

• The BCCI's domestic tournament for Under-23 cricketers is named the C. K. Nayudu Trophy in his honour.

NOTE

• India played its first Test match in 1932 and won its first Test in 1952 (against England at Chennai). India's first ODI captain was Ajit Wadekar (1974).

question: Which social reformer from South India founded the Self Respect Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is EV Ramaswamy Naicker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker, popularly known as "Periyar", founded the "Self-Respect Movement" in 1925 in the Madras Presidency (Tamil Nadu). The movement aimed at achieving a society based on equality, self-respect and rationalism, opposing caste discrimination, untouchability and Brahminical dominance. (आत्म-सम्मान आंदोलन — पेरियार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Periyar championed women's rights, rationalism and social justice, and was a key figure in the Dravidian movement.

• He is often called the "Father of the Dravidian Movement".

NOTE

• Other social reformers of South India: Sri Narayana Guru (Kerala), Jyotiba Phule (Maharashtra, Satyashodhak Samaj) also worked for the depressed classes in the broader reform movement.
